name: LZSSE-SIMDe
listed_description: A portable SIMD implementation of LZSSE compression.
reason: README only shows parity with upstream LZSSE when SSE4.1 is native (LZSSE2 compress 87.18 s vs 86.33 s, decompress 0.55 s both; LZSSE8 decompress 0.45 s vs 0.44 s, avg of 5 runs on raspbian-jessie-lite-20151121.tar.xz, g++ 10, no CPU model) and slower numbers when SSE4.1 is emulated (-msse2 decompress 13.70 s vs 0.55 s). It states upstream cannot run without SSE4.1, so no baseline numbers exist, and makes no faster-than claim. It is a SIMDe port of the already catalogued LZSSE (ConorStokes/LZSSE), whose own faster-than-LZ4-HC evidence is the lzbench row.

name: smaz
reason: README gives only compression-ratio percentages on example strings (for example 'the end' compressed by 58%, 'This is a small string' by 50%) and the unnumbered statement that zlib will usually not compress text shorter than 100 bytes. No speed numbers and no benchmark against a named baseline in the README, repo page or any linked benchmark; the only speed figures found by search (PySmaz, a Python port) belong to a different project and show zlib far ahead on 5 MB inputs.

name: squash
listed_description: Compression abstraction library, complete with some
reason: Squash is a plugin abstraction layer over other codecs; its README and repo page contain no speed claim or numbers about Squash itself. The separate quixdb/squash-benchmark repo benchmarks the plugged-in codecs (results live on a blocked github.io site and are not in the repo), so any winner there belongs to the individual codecs, not to Squash.

name: Zlib
listed_description: Massively spiffy yet delicately unobtrusive compression library
reason: zlib is the incumbent baseline other catalogue entries beat; its README, FAQ and repo page make no comparative speed claim. The only numeric speed statement is in ChangeLog ('Speed up software CRC-32 computation by a factor of 1.5 to 3'), which compares against an earlier zlib release, not a named external baseline. In the lzbench 2.4 table zlib 1.3.2 -1 (89.0 / 297 MB/s) is slower than zlib-ng, libdeflate, LZ4, Snappy, LZO and zstd, so no one claims it wins.
